# Fable V3 — integrated revision of V2 (parent), Flight-Dynamics-II-ready evidence package

**Status:** design revision only. No wind-tunnel, whirling-arm, bench or flight measurement exists for this aircraft. Every number below is either a design assumption [A], an external hand/AVL-class calculation from assumptions [C], or UNKNOWN. Nothing is a measured result [M]. No construction or crewed-flight clearance is proposed or implied. This is a modern researcher-assisted round; the analysis methods named here were not in the 1898 packet.

## 1. What changed from V2 and why

The evaluator found three unresolved interfaces in V2 (tail sweep/clearance, fuel centroid outside its box, transverse shaft vs bracing) and no reconciled whole aircraft including the V6/V8 propeller work. V3 resolves each by geometry, then re-closes the mass ledger, computes a shape-model inertia tensor, recomputes trim by the same method as V2 (so the evaluator can reproduce it), and specifies the analysis/test matrix needed for eight roots.

- **Tail clearance (C3-01/02):** inboard edge of each all-moving half moved from |y| 0.45 to 0.55 (tip 2.75→2.85, area 4.60 m² unchanged), giving a 0.15 m gap to the frame side. A new frame station at x 5.65 (nodes F25–F28) carries the torque-tube bearings so that no diagonal wire crosses the tube. Horn radius reduced 0.30→0.25 m because the V2 lower horn tip (z 0.475) sat below the lower longeron (z 0.488 at x 5.65) — a collision V2 did not catch. Full-travel sweep envelope is tabulated in the JSON: x 5.41–6.37, z 0.67–0.98 at −16°/+8° absolute; fin (z ≥ 1.20, y = 0) and rudder (x ≥ 6.60) are not reached.
- **Fuel (C3-03):** tank centroid corrected to (1.575, 0, 1.05), inside the box z 0.95–1.15; tank structure 4 kg and fuel 16 kg split; full/empty CG extremes given.
- **Transmission/brace (C3-04):** new frame verticals at x 1.85 (F29–F32) so the side-face diagonals of bay 1.15–2.55 terminate at a post, and the transverse shaft passes through a bearing in that post at z 0.80. At the interplane post lines y ±0.90 a spruce cross-member at (1.85, ±0.90, 0.80) splits the fore-aft diagonals into two half-bays and carries the shaft clamp. Outboard bevel boxes and hubs at y ±1.60 are now carried by explicit outrigger struts (new item P17) from the rear spar nodes (2.55, ±1.60, 0 / 1.85) to the hub bearing (3.00, ±1.60, 0.80). V1 blocker B-4 is therefore closed geometrically; strength remains UNKNOWN.
- **V6 propeller adoption (C3-05):** 2-blade, D 2.30 m, 600 rpm, hub radius 0.10 m, V6-RN-TE section family, assembly mass 12 kg (V3b proposal) are adopted because they are mechanically compatible with the V2 side-by-side hubs at (3.00, ±1.60, 0.80). Propeller A (+ω x̂) is assigned to the left hub, B to the right ("tops move outboard"). Not adopted: coaxial layout (not compatible), any thrust claim (V6 T7 not run), reduction ratio (engine speed UNKNOWN). The V6 provisional chord table is carried with its provisional flag.
- **CG recovery (C3-06):** the +7 kg propeller mass and +5.5 kg of new structure at x 1.85–3.0 moved the CG aft to 36% chord; the pilot seat datum was moved forward 0.15 m and the engine 0.10 m to return to 32.8% chord. This is a bookkeeping consequence, not a static-margin target chosen in isolation; the neutral point remains an estimate to be replaced by AVL and by test.
- **Mass (C3-07):** all-up 295 → 309.5 kg. Every mass is still an unweighed assumption.

## 2. Trim recompute (same method as V2, [C], not validation)

At 13 m/s, ρ 1.225, W 3036 N, S 42 m², CG (1.557, 0, 0.766): required CL 0.698; wing α ≈ 5.4° body (arc zero-lift −5.7°, CLα 3.8/rad biplane-corrected); wing Cm_ac −0.157 → −1329 N·m; lift offset (0.328−0.25)·1.85 = 0.144 m → +436 N·m; thrust 420 N at 0.034 m above CG → −14 N·m; tail must supply +907 N·m at arm 4.34 m → tail lift −209 N, CL_t −0.44, tail deflection ≈ −3.0° from rigging (absolute −7.0°), within the −16/+8 absolute travel. Static margin by the V2 estimator ≈ 7% chord at mid-CG, 5% at aft seat stop, before slipstream and body effects, which are not modelled and could be of either sign. These numbers exist only so the evaluator can reproduce them; they are not a trim verdict.

## 3. Inertia and sign convention

Body frame B: x aft, y right, z up, origin at front cross-member centre. Moments: L, M, N positive right-hand about +x, +y, +z, so **positive M is nose-up when x is aft and z is up? No —** with x aft and z up, a right-hand rotation about +y (from z toward x) drops the nose; therefore in this frame positive M is **nose-down**. To keep the V2 statement "pitching moment positive nose-up", V3 reports aerodynamic pitching moment as M_aero = −M_B and states this explicitly; the state-matrix work in §6 must be done in a standard flight frame (x forward, z down) obtained by the rotation R = diag(−1, 1, −1), under which Ixz changes sign. Inertia convention: I_xx = Σm(y²+z²) etc.; products reported as P_xz = Σm·x·z (positive-definite convention), so the tensor off-diagonal is −P_xz. Intrinsic inertias come from named shape models (plate, rod, box, rotation-averaged 2-blade rod); they are not measured and are not inferred from centroids alone. Uncertainty ±30% on each diagonal, ±100% on P_xz, until the bifilar/compound-pendulum test T-M2 is run.

## 4. Analysis and test matrix, roots, and the unstable-mode contingency

States: V ∈ {12, 13, 16} m/s × CG ∈ {30.7, 32.8, 34.6 %c} × power {on at 10.7 kW-equivalent thrust, off/windmilling}. Steady derivatives by AVL (or equivalent vortex-lattice) with the coordinates in the JSON; body/post/skid side-force by component build-up flagged as [A]; C_Lα̇ and C_mα̇ can **not** come from steady AVL — they are carried as an interval from a lag-of-downwash model [A] and are settled only by forced-oscillation of a scale model (T-A3). Propulsion derivatives (C_Tu, C_mT, slipstream ΔC_Lt) from the V6 T7 blade-element run plus tethered thrust/hinge-moment test (T-P2). Eight roots are to be computed as eigenvalues of the 4×4 longitudinal and lateral A matrices built from those dimensional derivatives and the tensor in §3; mode labelling by eigenvector content. Preliminary pre-screen values (labelled [C], from V2 derivatives, useful only to size the test bandwidth): short-period ω_n ≈ 4.5 rad/s, ζ ≈ 0.9; phugoid period ≈ 6 s, ζ ≈ 0.1 (from the L/D ≈ 7 assumption); roll time constant ≈ 0.07 s; Dutch-roll ω_n ≈ 1.0 rad/s with damping UNKNOWN (C_nr not estimated); spiral UNKNOWN (C_lβ ≈ 0 with no dihedral, sign then set by C_lr/C_lp and body contributions). None of these is a stability verdict.

Contingency if the lateral screen shows a divergent spiral or under-damped Dutch roll: fin extended from z 1.80 to 2.20 (+0.48 m², +1.3 kg at (6.0, 0, 1.7)), which moves the CG aft 0.019 m; compensated by 0.08 m forward seat travel, no power change, trim tail deflection changes by ≈ −0.3°. Second candidate held in reserve: 2° dihedral on P01 only (mass-neutral, changes spar geometry and the ground-clearance schedule). If the aft-CG short period or phugoid fails, the seat aft stop is limited to 32.8% and the retest repeated; no other longitudinal change is proposed until the C_mα̇ interval is narrowed.
